turns.content: An unknown trisubstituted aromatic compound gives 1H NMR signals at 7.1 ppm (1H, s), 7.0 ppm (1H, d), 6.7 ppm (1H, d), 3.7 ppm (3H, s), and 2.3 ppm (3H, s). Calculate the total integration and separate the aromatic from the non-aromatic signals.
Focus on the two non-aromatic three-proton singlets. What common substituent environments usually give resonances near 3.7 ppm and 2.3 ppm?
Interpret the three distinct one-proton aromatic signals, including the singlet-plus-two-doublets pattern. What does it imply about substitution and symmetry on the benzene ring?
Assign the 3.7 ppm and 2.3 ppm singlets using chemical shift, integration, and multiplicity. Does the spectrum support a methoxy-plus-aryl-methyl combination or two aryl methyl groups?
Combine the non-aromatic assignments with the unsymmetrical three-proton aromatic pattern and identify the best-supported compound by name.

Test that assignment against a chloromethoxyphenol and against chloroxylenes. Which spectral features conflict with a phenolic OH or with two aryl-methyl groups, and what ordinary uncertainty remains from chemical-shift variation or peak overlap?

Perform a final internal check: account for all nine integrated protons and explain why the oxygen-shifted singlet and three distinct aromatic resonances are mutually consistent with the proposed structure.
Give the final compound name and a concise spectral justification based on the aromatic pattern and both non-aromatic singlets.
